title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: Misdeclared Goods and Excluded Perils
content:
Certain losses fall outside every tier of `Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims`, however broad the cover. They arise from what the goods really were, or from what caused the loss.

## Misdeclared goods

When the dangerous-goods acceptance for the goods carries a misdeclaration penalty, a claim on those goods is rejected as misdeclared cargo. This holds under every tier, since the goods carried were not the goods the line accepted.

## Excluded perils

Where the loss was brought about by inherent vice of the goods, or by packing on the claimant's side that was insufficient, the loss is an excluded peril under every tier.

**Whose word decides.** The finding that a loss arose from insufficient packing or inherent vice rests on the survey report that the claims department has recorded. The claimant's own account, taken alone, never establishes it, whether to find the exclusion or to rule it out.

## Points of judgement

| What the records show | Consequence |
|---|---|
| The dangerous-goods acceptance for the goods carries a misdeclaration penalty | rejection as misdeclared cargo, under any tier |
| The recorded survey report finds insufficient packing by the claimant | excluded peril, under any tier |
| The recorded survey report finds inherent vice | excluded peril, under any tier |
| Only the claimant's statement speaks to packing or inherent vice | no finding of an excluded peril rests on it |

- *The claimant holds `AHL CargoCare Total`, the broadest tier. Does that protect goods whose acceptance carries a misdeclaration penalty?* No. The rejection applies under every tier.
